column2: They purify with the sieve that beloved bay-brown one, who goes with exhilaration around all the gods.
Of the pressing stalk — let the mortal not desire that speech; drive away the grudging dog, as the Bhrigus smote the sacrifice-spoiler.
The great, set in food, flows toward dear things, the names in which he grows; he, the all-seeing, mounted the all-turning chariot of the great Sun.
May the unurged drops run on for us, sounding, bay, great among the gods; may the strengths that devour the niggardly be ours; may our thoughts win.
This honeyed one roared in the vessel, Indra's thunderbolt, the body of bodies; the good-milking, ghee-dripping cows run to the truth, with milk.
The drop has gone forth to the appointed place of Indra; the friend does not break the friend's promise; Soma flows into the vessel by the hundred-course path, as a man with young women.
The upholder of heaven flows, the skilful essence, the skill of the gods, to be rejoiced in by men; the bay, released like a swift horse, you vainly make strength in the rivers.
The bull of thoughts flows, the seer, Soma, the day-crosser of dawns and heaven; he roared in the vessels at the breath of the rivers, entering Indra's heart with the wise.
For him seven cows yielded thrice the true mixture in the highest sky; the other four worlds he made lovely for adornment when he grew by the truths.
Flow around for Indra, well pressed, Soma; let disease be with the demons; may the double-dealers not delight in your essence; may the drops here be rich in wealth.
The red Soma, the bull, the bay, has been pressed, like a wondrous king; he has roared to the cows; purified, he passes the sheep's wool and sits in the ghee-rich nest like a falcon.
The honeyed drops have run toward the god, the cows have come to us; sitting on the grass, with the udder-gifts, the speaking ones put on the cleansing.
They anoint, they adorn, they decorate; they lick the skill, they anoint with honey; at the breath of the river, the golden-purified take the bull flying in the waters.
Your filter is spread out, O lord of prayer; the mighty one, you pervade all the limbs on every side; the unheated body does not attain it; only the cooked, carrying, reach it together.
Let these pressed bay drops go to Indra the bull; drops born in the hearing, finders of heaven.
Run forth, Soma, wakeful; flow around for Indra, O drop; bring splendid strength, the heaven-finder.
Friends, sit down; sing to him who is being purified; adorn him with offerings like a child for glory.
Sing, friends, to him being purified for exhilaration; sweeten him with offerings and songs like a child.
The child of the great ones, urging the light of truth, has become dear to all, in two ways.
Flow, drop, with streams and strength for the feast of the gods; come to our vessel, honeyed Soma, sit.
Soma, purifying with a wave, runs through the sheep's wool; flowing at the front of speech, roaring.
A word is spoken to the purifying creator Soma; he is pleased with the songs, like a payment.
Drop, press for us a rich-in-cattle, rich-in-horses wealth, O skilful; hold the pure color in the cows.
The voices have praised you for us, the finder of wealth; we clothe your color with cows.
The beloved bay-colored flows swiftly over crookednesses; flow to the singers heroic glory.
Soma, purifying, flows around the honey-dropping vessel; the seven voices of the sages praise.
Flow, most honeyed, for Indra, O Soma, the most skilled exhilaration, the great, most heavenly exhilaration.
O lord of food, shine great splendor and fame, O god, the god-seeking; open the middle vessel, young one.
Come, pressers, pour around, like a swift horse, a hymn that crosses the air, wood-sprinkled, water-leaping.
This exhilaration-dropping, thousand-streamed bull, milking heaven, bearing all wealth.
He is pressed who leads wealth, riches and refreshments, Soma of the good dwellings.
You, indeed, O flowing one, most splendid, proclaim the divine births for immortality.
This one, pressed with the stream, flows through the sheep's wool, most exhilarating, sporting like a wave of the waters.
He who cut the cows that were within the rock by his might, who spread toward the cattle-pen full of cattle and horses — break, bold one, like armor. Om; break, bold one, like armor.
Bring us, Indra, the eldest, the mightiest, abundant fame, that we may hold, O thunderbolt-handed, you who have filled both worlds, O fair-jawed.
Indra is king of the world and the peoples, on the earth whose form is of all shapes; from it he gives treasures to the giver and urges bounty even to the near praised.
Of whom these dust-yoked ones are the delight to the toiling people, the forest, the sun; the great, pleasing one of Indra.
Loosen from us the highest bond, Varuna, the lowest below, and the middle; then, O Aditya, in your law may we be sinless toward Aditi.
With you, flowing Soma, may we always choose what is done in battle; may Mitra, Varuna, Aditi, the river, earth and heaven honor it.
Make this bull the one for me.
May you, finder of wealth, flow around for us, for worshipful Indra, for Varuna, for the Maruts.
By this, in the lord, we win all the splendors of men, desiring to win them.
I am the first-born of truth, the name of immortality, before the gods; whoever gives me, he indeed helps me; I eat the eater of food.
You held this in the black and red and gray cows — the shining milk.
The foremost dappled one made the dawns shine; the bull measures out in the worlds, seeking strength; the magicians measured by his magic; the fathers, seeing men, placed the embryo.
Indra alone is united with the two bay horses, bound by speech; Indra the thunderbolt-bearer, golden.
Protect us, Indra, in contests and in thousandfold battles, O fierce one, with fierce helps.
Whose name is Prathas and Saprathas; the oblation of the anushtubh offering; from Dhatar's brightness and from Savitar and Vishnu, Vasishtha brought the Rathantara.
O Vayu with your team, come to the soma-offering; I have brought the bright one for you; you will go to the house of the presser.
When you were born, unprecedented, bounteous, for the slaying of Vritra, then you spread the earth and also propped up heaven.
In me splendor, and fame, and the milk of the sacrifice; may Parameshthi Prajapati make firm in heaven, like the sky.
May your milks and strengths come together, and your manly powers that overcome rivals; swelling, O Soma, for immortality, hold the highest fames in heaven.
You, Soma, brought forth all these plants, you the waters, you the cows; you spread the wide air; you with light drove away the darkness.
I praise Agni, the household priest, the god, the priest of the sacrifice, the invoker, the best bestower of jewels.
They thought of the first name of the cows, the highest name of the people, thrice seven; knowing them, the lands praised; the red cows appeared with glory.
Some come together, some approach; the rivers fill the same wide space; to that bright, shining one, the son of waters, the waters come.
The auspicious young woman has come forth, she seeks to raise the banners of the day; she has become the auspicious settler, night of the whole world.
Now to the great, strong, ruddy one, to Jatavedas, our word goes at the ritual; a new, pure thought for Vaishvanara flows like Soma, lovely, for Agni.
May all the gods hear my sacrifice, both heaven and earth, and the son of waters, my thought; let me not speak words of yours that are to be refused; may we rejoice in your nearest favors.
May heaven and earth give me glory; glory be mine from Indra and Brihaspati; may I find the glory of Bhaga; may my glory not be released; may I be a glorious speaker in this assembly.
Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, which the thunderbolt-bearer did first: he slew the serpent, released the waters, and split the flanks of the mountains.
I am Agni, Jatavedas by birth; ghee is my eye, immortality in my mouth; threefold light, measure of the space, unceasing light, I am the whole offering.
Agni protects the first station of the sage; the great one protects the course of the sun; Agni protects the seven-headed one at the navel.
They shine, Agni, kindled, brilliant; the tongue moves within the mouth; you, Agni, finder of wealth, have given us with milk wealth and splendor to see.
Spring is a delight; summer is a delight; the rains, then the autumns; winter and the cold season are a delight.
The Person has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet; he pervaded the earth on all sides and stood beyond it by ten fingers.
Three quarters rose up, the Person; one quarter of him remained here again; thereby he strode out in all directions, to what eats and what does not eat.
The Person alone is all this, what has been and what will be; all beings are a quarter of him; three quarters of immortality are in heaven.
So great is his greatness, and the Person is greater than that; he is also lord of immortality, which rises beyond through food.
From him Viraj was born, and from Viraj the Person; born, he extended beyond the earth, behind and before.
I think of you, heaven and earth, good nourishers, who spread immeasurably, a league beyond; heaven and earth, be kind and free us from sin.
Your two bay horses, Indra, and your beard are tawny; the seers praise you, the men, forest-dwellers.
By whatever radiance of gold, or radiance of cows, by the radiance of truth and prayer, with that we unite ourselves.
Indra, grant us that force; you indeed rule over this great one, O praised one; grant us power, manly strength, durable and strengthening, and easy slaying of foes among the Vritras.
Come, with bulls and calves, bearing all forms, the two-milking ones; may this wide, broad place be yours; may these waters be good for drinking here.
O Agni, you purify our lives; bring us energy and food; drive far away evil dogs.
May the shining, great one drink the honeyed soma, giving unharmed life to the lord of the sacrifice; urged by the wind, he guards by himself, nourishes offspring, and shines in many ways.
The wondrous face of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuna and Agni; the Sun, the soul of what moves and what stands, has filled heaven, earth and air.
This dappled bull has come, he sat before his mother, and the father, going to heaven.
Within moves its light, breathing out from breath; the great one has lit up the sky.
The thirty-seat abode shines; speech is set for the bird; in front of the dwelling by days.
Like thieves the stars go away with the nights, before the all-seeing Sun.
His banners have been seen, his rays spread over the people, shining like fires.
You are swift, seen by all, the light-maker, O Sun; you illuminate the whole bright sky.
You rise facing the clans of the gods, facing men, facing all, to be seen in heaven.
By the eye, O purifier, by which you look on the people, bearing them, you, Varuna, behold.
You go up to heaven, measuring the broad space with days, beholding creatures, O Sun.
The Sun yoked seven bright mares of the chariot; with them he goes, yoked by themselves.
Seven bay horses carry you on your chariot, god Sun, the all-seeing with flame-hair.
Know, bounteous one, know the way; you have praised the directions; teach, lord of powers, O rich in wealth, the ancient ones.
You with your helps, as the shining drop of heaven; O wise one, awaken us for splendor and food, Indra.
So indeed, powerful one, for wealth and strength, thunderbolt-bearer; strongest, thunderbolt-bearer, you shine; greatest, thunderbolt-bearer, you shine; come, drink, rejoice.
Know, for wealth, heroic strength; be lord of strengths according to your will; greatest, thunderbolt-bearer, you shine, who are the strongest of heroes.
You who are the greatest of the bounteous, shining like a ray; O knowing one, lead us; Indra is to be known; praise him.
For the powerful rules; we call on him for help, the victor unconquered; may he bring us heaven beyond hatred, the skill, the meter, the great truth.
We call on Indra for the winning of wealth, the victor unconquered; may he bring us heaven beyond hatred; may he bring us heaven beyond hatred.
Of your ancient one, O stone-bearer, the shining ray for exhilaration; place us in favor, O Vasu; O strongest, fullness is praised; the powerful alone now takes up that new.
O lord of the people, Vritra-slayer, we two shall speak in battles; the hero who goes among the cattle, a friend, a good comforter, not two-faced.
So indeed, O Agni; so indeed, Indra; so indeed, Pushan; so indeed, the gods. Om, so indeed, the gods.
Sing to him, men, the purifying drop; he seeks the gods.
The Atharvans have mixed milk with honey for you; the god-seeking for the god.
Flow for us for the welfare of the cow, the people, the horse; for the welfare of the plants, O king.
With shining light and sounding grace the bright somas mixed with milk.
Urged on by the urgers, the racer has stepped to the strength, sitting like the pious.
Straight, Soma, for welfare, joining by day, seer, flow for the Sun to see.
The courses of you, flowing seer, have been released, O racer, like horses seeking fame.
Toward the honey-dripping vessel they were released in the sheep's wool; the thoughts desired.
The drops go to the sea, like cows to the stall, reaching the womb of truth.
O god, you seek for us the wide, famed, great heroic strength, Agni.
Mitra and Varuna, sprinkle our pasture with ghee and our realms with honey, O skilled ones.
